evidence.source: 《字源》, edited by 李學勤, 2012; inspected scan at /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-1289/source.png; continued at page-1290/source.png
evidence.field: PDF pp. 1289–1290, printed pp. 1274–1275, 巴 entry and continuation; scan pixels inspected
evidence.text: The visible headword is 巴, read bā. The entry describes it as picturing a snake with a large mouth, says its earliest form is the Shuowen small-seal form, and proposes a giant snake as its original meaning. It cites the Shanhaijing and Shuowen accounts. The entry’s listed forms are Shuowen seal, Han, Han, and regular script; no oracle-bone form is shown here. The continuation distinguishes later meanings such as 尾巴 and 下巴 as phonetic loans unrelated to that proposed original meaning. These are the book’s claims, not independent confirmation of 巴’s early referent.

evidence.field: 爸 entry; graph description, Shuowen status, and cited dictionary gloss
evidence.text: The entry says 爸 is not recorded in Shuowen, describes the standard graph as 父 above 巴, and cites 集韻: 爸，爹、父也. It lists dictionary records but does not date the first physical occurrence of the complete graph.

evidence.source: 廣雅 via 識典古籍
evidence.text: The inspected text groups 爸, 爹, and 㸙 under 父也. This is evidence for a written lexical gloss in the transmitted text; it does not date a physical witness or establish when the graph was formed.

evidence.source: Deng Li and Huang Renxuan, Language Research 46(3), 2026
evidence.field: historical uses and attributed lexical history
evidence.text: The article calls 爸 a later graph and reports its earliest textual record as the Guangya gloss 爸，父也, which the authors date to the Three Kingdoms period. It separately reports 爸爸 and 阿爸 as father terms in Qing texts, and discusses Tang 郎爸/郎罢 as a lexical form. The authors argue that the father word’s sound derives from 父; that is their lexical-history proposal, separate from the graph’s component analysis. The cited underlying historical works were not independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 现代汉语“父亲”称谓系统音义关系研究

evidence.source: Qiu Yansui, Bulletin of Chinese, no. 48 (2010), pp. 245–246
evidence.field: section 7, 父聲系、巴聲系; sound-role statement and Middle Chinese readings
evidence.text: In the sentence 从巴得声的「爸」是「父」的后起字, the printed sound referent is 巴 itself: Qiu says 爸 takes its sound from 巴 and is a later graph for 父. His section groups the 父 and 巴 sound series for comparison and lists 爸 with fanqie 必駕切 and 捕可切. This supports an attributed phonetic analysis, not the date of the 父+巴 graph. The reference is Qiu’s discussion, not independent inspection of an early 爸 inscription.
evidence.title: 從漢語詞族看上古聲母的擬音問題

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 爸 entry, reporting Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003
evidence.field: graphic component analysis and Old Chinese readings
evidence.text: The entry explicitly analyzes 爸 as a phono-semantic compound: semantic 父 and phonetic 巴. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system it gives 巴 *praː and 爸 *praːs, with an additional 爸 reading *baʔ. The *praː/*praːs comparison is a source-reported historical sound comparison; it does not identify 巴’s original depicted object or name.
evidence.title: 爸 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 𤕕 variant entry; reported Zhengzitong explanation
evidence.text: The entry quotes a Zhengzitong account that an elder was called 八八 or 巴巴 in a non-Chinese language and that 父 was later added to write 爸. This is a historical lexicographic proposal, not independently verified evidence for the source language, borrowing, or graph chronology.
evidence.title: 𤕕 (爸) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Cao Dingyun, Yindu Xuekan 2013(4), Wanfang abstract
evidence.field: abstract; disputed interpretation of oracle-bone forms identified as 巴
evidence.text: Cao argues that oracle-bone forms read 巴 depict a pregnant woman and rejects the snake interpretation. The abstract identifies the snake account as an opposing view and disputes its connection to the oracle-bone forms. This establishes a modern scholarly disagreement, not a settled reading of those forms or proof of 巴’s original referent.
evidence.title: 再论甲骨文“巴”字是“妇女怀孕”之状——兼答谷斌、刘雁二同志之“商榷”

evidence.text: The page transmits 巴, 虫也。或曰食象蛇。象形 and Duan Yucai’s note connecting the snake statement to the Shanhaijing. This documents a historical dictionary account; it does not establish that the original graph depicted a snake.

No consulted source provides a securely dated physical witness for the complete graph 爸. The Three Kingdoms dating is a scholarly report about the Guangya textual record, not a date for the surviving physical witness or for the graph’s formation.

The source analyses of 巴’s early identity and original referent conflict: 字源 and the transmitted Shuowen tradition give a snake account, while Cao Dingyun argues that forms read 巴 depict a pregnant woman. Neither the inspected evidence settles the early form’s identity or original referent.

Wiktionary’s Proto-Sino-Tibetan *p/ba proposal and the 2026 article’s claim that 爸 preserves a father-word pronunciation related to 父 are not independently established here. Treat them as attributed lexical proposals, distinct from the graph’s 巴 sound-component analysis.
